candidates.business_summary: We are China's largest and most vertically integrated DRAM maker - we research, design and manufacture the memory that goes into servers, PCs and phones, and we are the world's fourth-largest DRAM producer at roughly 7.7% global share. We make money selling memory bits into a commodity market where price is set by industry-wide supply, so our earnings swing violently with the cycle: we lost RMB 7.87B in 2024, earned our first annual profit of RMB 1.87B on RMB 61.79B revenue in 2025, and have guided first-half 2026 revenue to RMB 110-120B with RMB 50-57B net profit. Our capacity is booked by Dell, HP and Lenovo through the end of 2027. The binding constraint on us is not demand or capital but export controls on the advanced lithography we need to keep shrinking nodes.

candidates.reason: Bucket 1 - relevant regardless of size. AD109 (Oxnimbi) would be the first oral drug for obstructive sleep apnea, with two positive Phase 3 trials and a PDUFA date of 2027-02-28. It is the largest single threat to the Inspire Medical (INSP) and ResMed (RMD) theses, both Core=Y in the Sleep subsector. Upsized IPO priced at the top of range ($16 vs $14-16 filed), $192M gross. Open classification question for JP: filed as Biopharma/Sleep, but the Sleep subsector currently sits under MedTech - alternative is Biopharma/Respiratory.
candidates.business_summary: We are trying to turn a device market into a drug market. More than 80 million US adults have obstructive sleep apnea and the standard of care is a CPAP machine that a large share of patients abandon, or surgery to implant a nerve stimulator - nobody has ever had a pill. Our lead candidate AD109 (aroxybutynin 2.5mg plus atomoxetine 75mg, branded Oxnimbi) is a once-daily oral tablet that maintains upper-airway tone pharmacologically; in the Phase 3 LunAIRo trial it cut apnea-hypopnea index by 46.8% at 26 weeks versus 6.8% on placebo, with no drug-related serious adverse events. We have no revenue and will make money by selling a branded prescription drug into a condition currently reimbursed as durable medical equipment, with an FDA decision due 2027-02-28. We raised $192M at $16 per share in our upsized Nasdaq IPO.

candidates.business_summary: We are the only American company manufacturing both DRAM and NAND flash memory at scale, selling into servers, PCs, phones, cars and industrial equipment under the Micron brand to OEMs and Crucial to consumers. Roughly three-quarters of our revenue is DRAM and one quarter NAND - in fiscal Q3 2026 that was $31.3B against $9.9B. High-bandwidth memory has reshaped the company: combined HBM, high-capacity DIMM and LP server DRAM revenue crossed $10B in fiscal 2025, a more than five-fold increase, and our 2026 HBM supply is fully committed before it is built. We still make money on the spread between a bit cost we control through process-node transitions and a bit price the industry sets, but HBM is contracted ahead per customer and consumes the wafer capacity that would otherwise make commodity DRAM - so it tightens our base market as a side effect.
